properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — surfaced 2026-08-11 checking `docs/requirements-coverage.md`'s deferrals against the code rather than trusting its status column. Nothing here is intent.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. HEAL-3 says the catalogue is 8 of 13, with `unreachable`, `weak_connection`, `missing_link`, `missing_entity` and `missing_embedding` deferred. Grepping the core: the only hits for those five are a MODULE COMMENT at `crates/reflow2-core/src/heal.rs:27-29` and unrelated `unreachable!()` macros. So the five are genuinely absent — confirmed, not assumed.

⭐ BUT THAT COMMENT IS ITSELF STALE, WHICH IS THE SHARPER FINDING. heal.rs:27-29 reads: "Deferred (need `dynograph-graph` or the LLM): dead_end / unreachable / disconnected_community / weak_connection / single_point_of_failure / missing_link…". Three of those — `dead_end`, `disconnected_community`, `single_point_of_failure` — ARE BUILT and were being proposed as fixes until PR #147 narrowed them this same session. A comment naming what is missing has kept naming things that arrived.

⭐⭐ AND HEAL-14'S BLOCKER HAS EXPIRED. The row reads "⬜ Missing-intermediate Component for hierarchy — matryoshka (needs `Component.level`)". `Component.level` EXISTS: 3AX-9 is ✅, `hierarchy_issues` and `MissingIntermediateLevel` are in `crates/reflow2-core/src/hierarchy.rs` (5 references), and `missing_intermediate_level` is surfaced as a gap by `detect_gaps`. So the DETECTOR fires and the REPAIR was never written — `heal.rs` has zero references to it. The stated reason for deferring is gone and nothing noticed. This is the same shape as `cap:what-next`, whose blocker also expired unnoticed and which turned out to be buildable the moment anyone looked.

⚠️ THE COUNTERWEIGHT, and it is not optional: PR #147 (merged today) REMOVED HEAL's ability to propose `generate_bridge`/`generate_owner` for `disconnected_community`/`dead_end`/`orphan`, because inventing a relationship nobody designed is not a repair. A `generate_component` for a missing intermediate level is EXACTLY THAT SHAPE — inventing a subsystem to sit between a system and a part. So HEAL-14 may not be "unblocked and buildable"; it may be "unblocked and now forbidden by a rule accepted hours ago". `req:a-repair-suggestion-never-proposes-fabrication` is accepted. That tension is the actual question here and it did not exist when the row was written.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) Fix the stale module comment and the stale HEAL-14 blocker note — pure record-keeping, costs nothing, and stops the next reader inheriting both errors.
(b) Decide HEAL-14 on the anti-fabrication rule: either the missing-intermediate repair is legitimate (the level is derivable from the two endpoints, not invented) or it is forbidden and the row should be RETIRED rather than left ⬜ forever.
(c) Retire the five never-built categories from the catalogue. The project's own test is "unused AND redundant → retire; unused AND not-redundant → defer, and say so" — nobody has re-asked which of the five is which since 2026-07-22.
(d) Nothing. 8 of 13 has been enough for every trial so far, and no friction report has asked for the missing five.

📌 THE META-POINT, which is the reason this node exists at all: `requirements-coverage.md` carries a BINDING deferral discipline — "a deferral that isn't written down is a silent stub, which this project treats as the same integrity breach as a silent drop." Three rows were checked today and three were wrong: SP-3b says ingest cannot be called from a session (it can), GS-17 says the polished PROMPT step is deferred (`gap_to_prompt` does it), 3AX-5 says TemporalFact usage is deferred (133 instances). The table goes stale in BOTH directions, and nothing computes on it. That is the argument for deferrals living where a detector can reach them — and equally the argument against trusting this table as the source for what to build.
properties.name: OPEN — HEAL's defect catalogue is 8 of 13, one deferral's blocker has EXPIRED unnoticed, and the module comment recording the gap is itself stale
properties.rationale: Checking three deferrals against the code found three stale rows and one expired blocker, plus a module comment that has kept naming built features as missing. The HEAL-14 question is genuinely live and genuinely changed: its blocker cleared, and hours later this session accepted a rule that may forbid the repair outright.
